parser.add_argument("--seed", choices=("alive", "ambiguous", "harvest"))
    parser.add_argument("--label")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    parser.phase = args.phase
    missing = [flag for flag in PHASE_REQUIRED_OPTIONS.get(args.phase, ())
               if getattr(args, flag) is None]
    if missing:
        parser.error(args.phase + " requires "
                     + ", ".join("--" + flag for flag in missing))
    case = _matrix_case_of(args.phase)
    if case is not None and args.boundary not in (None, case):
        parser.error(args.phase + " proves the " + case + " case derived"
                     " from its name, not --boundary " + args.boundary)
    try:
        require(os.uname().nodename == "crq-probe",
                "proof driver only runs on the disposable crq-probe guest")
        if args.phase == "prepare":
            payload = phase_prepare(args)
        elif args.phase in ("drain-alive", "drain-ambiguous"):
            payload = drain_refuse_phase(args)
evidence.reason: The parser accepts `--seed` independently of the phase, and `drain-alive` and `drain-ambiguous` both dispatch to the same `drain_refuse_phase(args)` handler with no seed/phase consistency check. Unlike the adjacent matrix-boundary guard, which rejects a conflicting `--boundary`, nothing prevents `drain-alive --seed ambiguous` from selecting the ambiguous probe while retaining the `drain-alive` phase label/evidence. Rejecting a mismatched seed before dispatch, or deriving it from the phase, is a small correctness fix.
